lines: $8Emily offered to weave flowers into my hair earlier... and Mayor Lewis insisted I sample the punch before I could even refuse...
Back where I came from, people either feared my presence or tried to use it. Here, they simply ask if I am enjoying the spring air...
$2I am... still learning how to exist in a place without an enemy to fight, {{playerName}}.
The seasons turn so gently here. No crises, no warnings—just music, blossoms, and neighbors gathering in good faith...
$1I used to think peace was an illusion meant for other people. Standing here today... I am grateful to have been proven wrong.
I still stand out like a shadow among all these bright spring colors, yet nobody seems to mind...
Knowing you are by my side makes it far easier to step out onto that field, {{playerName}}. Whenever you are ready, I am yours.
Once, I measured every room by exits, threats, and the eyes watching me. Today, I barely noticed the crowd gathered on the ridge.
$1All I see is the spring light in your hair, {{playerName}}.Let the valley celebrate as it pleases. My world begins and ends right beside you—shall we dance?
Glowing lights drifting across the dark water... For a moment, I braced for the cold pull of the Lifestream...
$4Yet there are no whispers here. No sorrow. Just quiet creatures following the tide.
It is a strange comfort to watch something luminescent that asks nothing of me.
Summer always seems to pass in the blink of an eye here. Back in my old life, I scarcely noticed the turning of the seasons—only the next mission.
$1Watching the jellies drift past reminds me that not every journey needs a destination.
$4Sometimes it is enough simply to exist.
$1The ocean air carries a chill tonight. Come, stand a little closer to me, {{playerName}}.
$1Everyone comes to the docks hoping to catch a glimpse of rare light... yet the only warmth I need is already standing beside me.
Once, I chased distant stars and impossible skies, believing greatness waited somewhere out in the dark.
$1Now I look at the reflection of the lights in your eyes, {{playerName}}, and wonder how I ever searched for anything else.
$3The jellies can take their time tonight. I am perfectly content right here with you.
Snow used to mean silence, isolation, and things best left buried... yet here, the cold only seems to draw everyone closer together.
Mayor Lewis explained the tradition of the secret gift exchange to me. Giving something thoughtfully, without expectation of reward or rank...
It is a simple custom, {{playerName}}, yet I spent far too long agonizing over what could possibly be worthy of a neighbor's kindness.
$6Another year has come full circle. A season ago, I stood at the edge of the square wondering if I even belonged at the table.
$3Today, Linus offered me spiced cider, and the children asked if I would help them build a snow-goon later.
$1I do not know if a man ever truly outruns his past, {{playerName}}... but days like this make me believe he can still build something good.
$1Your hands are cold, {{playerName}}. Here—let me warm them for a moment before the feast begins.
$3Everyone around the square is celebrating the blessings of the past year... yet no gift under that star could ever compare to coming home to you every evening.
$6Let the town exchange their ribbons and parcels. I stopped wishing for anything the day you agreed to share your life with me.
$3You are my hearth in the dead of winter, {{playerName}}—the only warmth I ever truly needed.
$1Stay close to me until the feast begins. I have no intention of letting you out of my sight today.
Everyone brings a single ingredient from their own harvest and drops it into one communal cauldron...
$2It requires an immense amount of trust that no one will add something ruinous.
$8I stood over my pantry for nearly an hour this morning, {{playerName}}. In all my years of combat, I have never felt quite so cautious over a simple vegetable.
There is something refreshing about a tradition where the highest stakes involve a Governor's palate rather than the fate of a city.
The ocean breeze is pleasant today, {{playerName}}. Have you added your contribution to the pot yet? Knowing your farm, I imagine it will outshine the rest of ours.
$1This coat was certainly not tailored for a summer beach gathering... yet I find I scarcely mind the heat when you are smiling like that.
$1Everyone keeps asking me what you brought for the soup, {{playerName}}. You have quite the reputation in this valley—and I cannot say I blame them for admiring you.
$1The Governor could declare the soup a masterpiece or a catastrophe, and I doubt I would even hear him.
$4All I can think about is how the sunlight catches your eyes against the water, {{playerName}}.
$1Once the ceremony ends, let us slip away from the crowd and walk along the shore together.
Carved gourds, paper ghosts, and skeletons behind iron bars...
$2In my past, illusions and monsters were things to be feared—or things I myself was accused of becoming.
Yet here, the villagers laugh, share spiced treats, and treat the dark as nothing more than a passing game. It is... oddly comforting.
$1I walked through the labyrinth earlier to ensure none of the younger villagers had lost their way.
$1The Wizard certainly has a flair for theatrical illusions, though I suspect he did not anticipate someone calmly inspecting his false walls.
$3Still, it is good to see everyone enjoying the autumn night without a single genuine threat in sight.
The shadows grow quite deep near the edge of the square tonight. I know well enough that these decorations pose no real danger...
$1Yet if you wish to use them as an excuse to stay close to my side, I certainly will not object.
$2Once, the dark held nothing for me save old ghosts and regrets I could not outrun.
$1Now, the only spell I am under is the warmth of your hand in mine, {{playerName}}.
$3Let the rest of the valley chase after golden pumpkins tonight. I have already taken the hand of the greatest treasure in all the valley.
$8Mayor Lewis asked if I intended to join the egg hunt this afternoon...
$8I declined—it hardly seemed honorable to bring years of field reconnaissance to a contest meant for children.
$4Even so, watching everyone gather over brightly painted shells...
$1It is refreshing to see a competition where nobody gets hurt.
$3Spring has returned to the valley, and with it, the town's most earnest tactical operation of the season.
$1Abigail passed me a moment ago looking as focused as a cadet before a live drill.
$1Give her a fair challenge out there today, {{playerName}}—I will be watching from the sidelines.
$1If you wish to compete in the hunt today, {{playerName}}, I will gladly hold onto your coat while you search.
$6Though between the two of us... if you happen to find a particularly well-hidden egg, I might just consider it a trophy worth keeping on our mantelpiece.
$1The whole square is buzzing over hidden prizes, yet I have no desire to look anywhere other than right beside me.
$4Every morning I wake up next to you feels like a small miracle I still have not quite earned...
$1Go enjoy the festivities if you wish—I will be right here, waiting to welcome you back.
$1Entire tables laid out with fresh harvests, hand-spun wool, and baked goods... Every stall here is proof of patient, honest work.
$1Earlier, a merchant challenged me to test my strength at his striking booth—I politely declined before I could break his mallet.
$1There is a quiet dignity in building things rather than tearing them down. I find myself admiring it more each day.
I paused near the fortune teller's tent a moment ago. She offered to read my destiny in her crystal ball.
I thanked her and walked on. I spent far too many years letting prophecies and old ghosts dictate my path.
Whatever tomorrow holds, {{playerName}}, I would rather choose it with my own two hands.
$1I already walked past your grange display earlier, {{playerName}}. Frankly, the judges might as well award you first place now and spare everyone the suspense.
$1Come find me once you have finished browsing the stalls—I have been eyeing one of those plush prizes at the star-token booth, and I intend to win it for you.
$1The music, the lanterns, the endless chatter of the fair... it all fades into a quiet hum the moment you step beside me.
$1Let the fortune teller keep her secrets—my future is standing right in front of me, holding my hand.
$1Take your time enjoying the festival, {{playerName}}. Simply watching you smile is more than enough for me.
Frozen lakes and biting winds once meant long marches and desolate terrain to me.
$4Yet here, the villagers carve sculptures out of the ice and gather around warm braziers simply to enjoy one another's company.
$1It takes a quiet kind of courage to find joy in the harshest season. It is... quaint.
I have spent my life training for split-second reflexes, yet watching Willy and Pam stare down an ice hole requires an entirely different discipline.
There is a calm, meditative patience to fishing in the winter quiet.
$1Perhaps one day you might teach me the proper technique, {{playerName}}—without resorting to cutting a wider hole in the ice.
$1Mind your footing near the edge of the ice, {{playerName}}—I would rather not have to dive into the lake after you today.
$1If you are entering the fishing contest, I will be right here keeping your coffee warm until the final whistle blows.
$1Everyone around the lake is bundled in wool and scarves, yet I scarcely feel the winter wind at all.
$3One look at you, {{playerName}}, and the entire frozen forest feels as warm as midsummer.
$6Let the others compete for trophies and honors. Having you by my side is the only victory I will ever need.
